gap: No result ChatGPT got works out how much of the pack each meter drains per month while the cart is stored. Counted against a Vatrer 48V 105Ah pack (5,376 Wh), the Victron SmartShunt and the Renogy 500A monitor (1 mA standby) each use about 0.7% a month. The Junctek KG140F, at its 0.9 W module-plus-display rating, would use about 12% a month. The LiTime RS485 display can switch the whole battery system off, so it adds nothing.
standout_why: The cited cartvoltage.com/best-lithium-battery-meter-golf-cart/ page already gives the inputs: Victron SmartShunt under 1 mA, and 0.4 W plus 0.5 W for the Junctek KG-F modules. It never turns them into Ah or % of a pack per month or per winter. It also gives no standby figure for the Renogy and does not mention the LiTime display's system shutdown. cartvoltage.com/golf-cart-battery-meter-wrong-lithium/ (in the results, not cited) gives a voltage-to-SOC table but no meter draw at all. The other results are battery pages and spec PDFs that give no meter standby figures.
decides: This mostly confirms ChatGPT's picks. The Renogy 500A ($87.99 at renogy.com) and the Victron SmartShunt draw the same 1 mA, so storage drain does not separate them. On a 105 Ah pack each loses under 0.72 Ah a month, about 3.4% over a 5-month winter. It does count against the cartvoltage 'best overall' Junctek KG140F if its display stays powered: about 12% of a 5.4 kWh pack a month, or about 60% over a 5-month winter, on the rival's own numbers. For LiTime GC Comm owners, the $56.99 RS485 display is the storage-safe choice because it can turn the pack off.
